confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from web search results and summaries of aggregators (Numbeo, MyLifeElsewhere, Expatistan, Traveltables) plus a few cafe and bar menu snippets. I did not open those pages myself. The Brno figures are crowd-sourced, partly dated and differ between sources. Numbeo showed about 200 CZK for an inexpensive meal, about 1,000 CZK for a three-course meal for two, and 47-58 CZK for a domestic draft. Cappuccino prices ranged from 71 to 99 CZK. I converted at roughly 21.7 CZK per USD, which is implied by aggregator conversions and is not an official rate. Cocktail evidence is mixed: a stale Expatistan guess of about 159 CZK, a few bar listings of about 205 CZK, and Super Panda Circus at about 9 USD. The cocktail anchor sits at about 3.2 times the beer price. Wine by the glass had little direct Brno data (roughly 80-150 CZK inferred from scattered snippets), so I set it at about 1.6 times the beer price. Hostel and hotel anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge and the city context. I searched no accommodation prices and inspected no listings, so they are the least certain. The FX figure is the latest RBA observation that the rba.gov.au search returned (18 Nov 2026). The 19 Nov rate was not yet available.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink use Brno-specific aggregator data. Brno is the Czech Republic's second city and a university and fair city, and its prices are somewhat below Prague's. Accommodation is scaled from other Central European second cities such as Krakow, Wroclaw and Bratislava, with a discount to Prague.
